edits.find: NordVPN manages one of the largest physical infrastructure footprints in the consumer privacy sector, operating more than 6,400 servers across 111 countries. Published independent benchmarks consistently demonstrate that NordLynx exhibits minimal throughput degradation, often preserving 85% to 92% of baseline internet speeds on low-latency regional hops.

edits.find: • Threat Protection Pro: Unlike basic DNS-level ad blockers, NordVPN's Threat Protection Pro functions as an endpoint security layer. edits.find: ExpressVPN, owned by Kape Technologies, maintains its operational headquarters in the British Virgin Islands (BVI). Like Panama, the BVI is an autonomous British Overseas Territory with its own judicial system and no statutory data retention mandates. In privacy litigation, local courts require a verifiable local criminal offense before entertaining international discovery requests, providing strong legal insulation for digital traffic records.
edits.replace: ExpressVPN has been owned by Kape Technologies since 2021 and is based in the British Virgin Islands (BVI), a British Overseas Territory. As with any provider, jurisdiction shapes which legal requests the company can receive, but its logging practices and audits are a more direct indicator of what data it could hand over.
edits.reason: Ownership sourced; unverified legal claims removed

edits.find: ExpressVPN was among the earliest providers to completely eliminate mechanical hard drives and solid-state drives across its entire server fleet. Its proprietary
edits.replace: ExpressVPN announced in April 2019 that all of its servers run only on RAM, making it one of the earlier providers to remove hard drives and SSDs from its VPN servers. Its proprietary

edits.find: Because RAM requires continuous electrical power to preserve stored bits, it is physically impossible for user connection logs, encryption keys, or forensic artifacts to persist across reboots. If physical hardware is seized by hostile actors or government authorities, no usable persistent data can be retrieved from the unpowered machine.
edits.replace: Because RAM needs continuous power to hold data, anything stored only in memory is lost when a server is rebooted or powered off. This limits what could be recovered from a seized machine, although it does not by itself prove what a running server does or does not record, which is why independent audits matter.

edits.find: Because NordVPN, ExpressVPN, and Surfshark operate exclusively on diskless RAM-only servers, powering down or disconnecting a server from its rack instantly wipes all volatile memory registers. Previous real-world server seizures involving ExpressVPN in Turkey demonstrated that investigators could extract zero customer activity logs or stored connection metadata, corroborating the validity of their documented no-logs architecture.
edits.replace: All three providers say they run RAM-only (diskless) servers, so data held only in memory is lost when a server is powered off. In a widely reported 2017 case, Turkish investigators seized an ExpressVPN server and found no logs, which ExpressVPN said supported its no-logs policy. That case predates ExpressVPN's 2019 move to RAM-only servers, and a single incident is not a guarantee for every provider or server.

edits.find: Modern online privacy requires moving past marketing hype and evaluating verifiable technical architecture. NordVPN, ExpressVPN, and Surfshark each deliver enterprise-grade encryption, independently audited no-logs operating policies, and diskless RAM server fleets that fundamentally outclass unsafe "free" alternatives. For pure speed and comprehensive advanced security modules, NordVPN remains the benchmark. For frictionless simplicity and router-level home protection, ExpressVPN excels. For multi-device households and unmatched economic value, Surfshark provides the strongest overall return on investment.
edits.replace: NordVPN, ExpressVPN and Surfshark all use modern encryption, say they run RAM-only servers, and have had their no-logs claims assessed by outside firms, which puts them ahead of unknown free VPN apps. NordVPN suits people who want a broad feature set; ExpressVPN stands out for its Lightway protocol and router options; Surfshark suits households with many devices. Check each provider's current prices, device limits and audit reports before buying, because these change often.
